stem:
What is the correct direction of flow of electrical impulses?

(Each option shows a chain of two neurons; in every neuron the cell body bears the bushy dendrites at one end and a long axon ending in fine axon terminals at the other end. Option A: in each neuron the dendrites/cell body are on the right and the axon terminal on the left, with the arrows pointing leftward. Option B: in each neuron the dendrites/cell body are on the left and the axon extends rightward to its terminal, with arrows pointing rightward, so the axon terminal of the first neuron faces the dendrites of the second. Option C: the neurons are laid out like B with dendrites/cell body on the left and axon terminal on the right, but the arrows point leftward (backward). Option D: the first neuron points dendrite-to-axon left-to-right but the second neuron is mirrored with its dendrites/cell body on the right, so the two axon terminals face each other, with arrows pointing rightward.)

options.label: A
options.text: The arrangement in which both neurons have dendrites on the right and arrows point to the left

options.label: B
options.text: The arrangement in which impulses pass dendrite to cell body to axon to axon terminal, and on to the dendrite of the next neuron, with arrows pointing to the right

options.label: C
options.text: The arrangement laid out dendrite-to-axon left-to-right but with the arrows pointing to the left

options.label: D
options.text: The arrangement in which the second neuron is reversed so the two axon terminals face each other
